chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Do not eat the jarith, nor the marmaahi, nor the taifi, nor the tihal, because it is the house of blood and a morsel of the devil.

key_terms.الْجِرِّيْث: A type of fish, often identified as the sturgeon or a similar large fish with hard scales.
key_terms.الْمَارْمَاهِي: A type of fish, often identified as the sturgeon or a similar species.
key_terms.بَيْتُ الدَّمِ: House of blood, a descriptive term indicating high blood content or a specific anatomical feature.
key_terms.طَائِفِيًّا: A type of fish, possibly referring to a specific species or a characteristic of floating/swimming.
key_terms.طِحَالًا: A type of fish, often identified as the sturgeon or a species with a specific texture.
key_terms.مُضْغَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ: Morsel of the devil, a metaphorical description indicating a quality of bloodiness or impurity.

ai.seo_question: What types of fish are prohibited from eating in Shia jurisprudence according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) prohibiting the consumption of jarith, marmaahi, taifi, and tihal, linking the ban to their physical nature as 'houses of blood' and 'morsels of the devil.' This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *khasais* (distinctive physical traits) as indicators of impurity or spiritual detriment, distinguishing these species from permissible fish. The description underscores a holistic view of diet where physical texture and blood content influence both ritual purity and spiritual well-being.
